newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up in slow trading on Thursday on overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at 19,110 yuan ($2,303) per tonne, rising 130 yuan. It opened at 19,100 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 19,050 and a high of 19,130.
November 1996 rose 50 to 18,980, December 190 to 19,050, January 1997 gained 120 to 19,110, March 100 to 19,120 and April 80 to 19,130. Total volume fell to 21,880 tonnes from 43,710.
Copper opened higher and moved in a narrow range at high levels for most of the session, traders said.
Despite the day's rises, traders said most investors stayed on the sidelines due to the uncertain short-term market trend.
"Retail investors dominated today's trade," one trader said. "Investors were mixed about the short-term trend."

"Many investors believe copper has lost the power to fall sharply despite long-term poor fundamentals given the losses in the past few months," a second trader said. "Investors would have little to gain by selling at this moment."
Traders said the low spot copper price in Shanghai was another factor preventing futures from plunging.
The price is now around 19,000 and 19,300 yuan.
Analysts expect Shanghai copper to move in a narrow range in the next few days.
Aluminium had only 250 tonnes of the November contract traded, which ended at 13,360 yuan per tonne, down 40 yuan.
